description: lib.rs line 32 documents 'jmap-cid-types  ← this crate (capability + sha256 type)' as the crate's role. PLAN.md §'What this crate is' item 1 (lines 26-30) leads with: '1. CidCapability — the value object of the urn:ietf:params:jmap:cid capability in the JMAP Session resource. Currently empty per the draft (§3) but #[non_exhaustive] per workspace policy.' PLAN.md §'Public API (current state)' line 82-85 then says: 'Still to come in a follow-up bead (bd:JMAP-v9py post-.14): pub struct CidCapability ...'. But: (1) v9py.14 is closed, supports_cid() landed at request.rs:226 as a Session-level helper that reads the capability map directly — no CidCapability struct is needed in the current call path. (2) No struct with that name exists in src/. The crate's family-position diagram and lead-item public-API description both point to a type that has not been written. Two viable cleanups: (a) write the CidCapability { /* empty */ } marker now in capability.rs as PLAN.md describes, consistent with MetadataCapability shape, OR (b) drop CidCapability from lib.rs and PLAN.md until/unless a concrete consumer needs it — supports_cid() works fine without a Rust type for the empty value object. Option (a) costs ~30 lines and aligns the type-crate family. Option (b) shrinks public surface. Either is fine — pick one and update the docs to match.
